rem:co2-lp-dual-shadow-prices:
Remark Shadow prices and why the symmetric (2,2) configuration wins. The LP dual of LP dual selects linear O{=}C{=}O geometry has three shadow prices:

  • y_{\sigma}: value of each \sigma-bond shared pair
  • y_{\pi}: value of each \pi-bond shared pair
  • y_{\mathrm{sym}}: value of symmetric bond placement (equal bonds to both oxygens)

The symmetric double-bond configuration (k_1, k_2) = (2, 2) wins over asymmetric alternatives (3, 1) or (1, 3) because:

  • Each double bond contributes 4 attractive crossings.
  • The symmetric arrangement minimises O_1-O_2 repulsion (protons are maximally separated).
  • The asymmetric (3, 1) configuration wastes one of oxygen's valence sites and places more electron density on one side, increasing e-e repulsion.
rem:co2-vsepr-and-per-bond-energy:
Remark VSEPR as \Phi_1 minimisation; per-bond energy by bond order. This is the braid-theoretic origin of VSEPR geometry. Minimising electron-pair repulsion is exactly \Phi_1 minimisation over strand orderings. The LP dual formalises the repulsion-minimisation principle as a linear program.

The binding energy per C=O bond is compared with:

  • CO triple bond: \approx 11.09\;\text{eV} \;\mathrm{eV} (3 bonds)
  • CO_2 double bond: \approx 8.28\;\text{eV} \;\mathrm{eV} (2 bonds)
  • The per-bond energy decreases with bond order: 11.09/3 \approx 3.70 versus 8.28/2 \approx 4.14 \;\mathrm{eV} per shared pair.
rem:co2-double-bond-symmetry:
Remark VSEPR molecular geometry from \Phi_1 minimisation. The LP dual for CO_2 provides a categorical derivation of VSEPR (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion) theory. The key correspondence is:

VSEPR concept Braid framework
Electron pair repulsion ee crossing (\sigma, q-eigenvalue) increases \Phi_1
Bond pair vs lone pair Shared trefoil (2 attractive crossings) vs retained trefoil (1 attractive crossing)
Geometric arrangement Strand ordering in H_{N}(q)
Energy minimisation \Phi_1 minimisation via LP dual

For CO_2:

  • 2 bond pairs (double bonds), 0 lone pairs on C
  • VSEPR predicts: linear, 180^\circ bond angle
  • LP dual confirms: placing O_1 and O_2 on opposite sides of C in the strand ordering minimises the O-O proton repulsion crossings

For H_2O:

  • 2 bond pairs (single bonds), 2 lone pairs on O
  • VSEPR predicts: bent, \approx 104.5^\circ
  • LP dual should show: lone pairs force the two H's into a non-symmetric strand arrangement

The braid framework derives geometric preferences from the Hecke algebra structure rather than postulating repulsion rules. Bond angles emerge as properties of the optimal strand ordering, not input parameters.
sec:ch4-computation-intro: Methane raises the coordination number from two to four. Methane CH_4 as a molecular braid joins a central carbon to four hydrogens by four shared trefoils on the molecular strand set. Among all ways of arranging the four bond strands, the LP cost is minimised by the S_4-symmetric strand orderings. This S_4 symmetry is read as the 109.5^\circ tetrahedral bond angle. The same \Phi_1 minimisation that produced linear CO_2 now selects the tetrahedral geometry of CH_4.
def:ch4-molecular-braid: Definition Methane CH_4 as a molecular braid. Methane CH_4 is the molecular braid of one carbon atom C(6, 6) and four hydrogen atoms H_1, H_2, H_3, H_4, each sharing one electron pair with the carbon (four single bonds).
rem:ch4-tetrahedral-from-phi1: Remark Tetrahedral geometry of methane from \Phi_1 minimisation.
prop:ch4-lp-dual-binding:
Proposition S_4-symmetric strand ordering minimises \Phi_1 for CH_4. Conditional on Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients. The LP dual of the CH_4 molecular braid in H_{26}(q) selects the S_4-symmetric strand ordering as the ground state. The four C--H bond energies are equal by symmetry.

The LP dual for CH_4 has the structure:

  \min_{\pi \in S_{26}} \; \Phi_1(\mathcal{M}(C, H_1, H_2, H_3, H_4; \pi))

The S_4 symmetry of the optimum means:

  1. Each C--H bond has the same traced volume \hat{V}_b.
  2. Each H--H repulsion has the same \Phi_1 penalty.
  3. The total binding energy is exactly 4 \times \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}^{CH}.

The LP dual shadow prices:

  • y_{CH}: marginal value of one C--H bond = single-bond dissociation energy
  • y_{HH}: repulsion penalty per H--H pair (6 pairs total)
  • y_{\mathrm{sym}}: symmetry premium — the S_4-symmetric arrangement is lower in \Phi_1 than any asymmetric alternative

The symmetry premium y_{\mathrm{sym}} > 0 is the braid-theoretic origin of the regular tetrahedron. Breaking S_4 symmetry (e.g., compressing one H--C--H angle) costs \Phi_1 through increased H--H repulsion.
rem:ch4-tetrahedral-symmetry:
Remark Tetrahedral geometry as S_4 symmetry of the LP dual. Methane's tetrahedral geometry (109.5^\circ bond angles) is a direct consequence of \Phi_1 minimisation. In the 26-strand braid, the optimal ordering distributes the four H atoms equidistant from each other in strand space. This corresponds to the vertices of a regular tetrahedron in physical space.

The computation establishes the mapping:

Braid quantity Physical quantity
Strand separation between H atoms H--C--H bond angle
\Phi_1 penalty per H--H pair Steric repulsion energy
S_4 orbit of optimal ordering Tetrahedral symmetry group T_d
Breaking S_4 (asymmetric ordering) Jahn--Teller distortion

For comparison, the same construction for NH_3 (nitrogen + 3 hydrogens) gives C_{3v} symmetry with a lone pair occupying the 4th tetrahedral site. This produces the observed pyramidal geometry with bond angles \approx 107.8^\circ. The lone pair acts as a "phantom hydrogen" in the strand ordering, occupying space but contributing no bonding crossings.

This establishes the computational programme: every small molecule's geometry is determined by the LP dual of its molecular braid, with no geometric input required.
def:h2o-molecular-braid: Definition Water H_2O as a molecular braid. Water H_2O is the molecular braid assembled from three sub-units — one oxygen O(8,8) (A+Z = 16+8 = 24 strands, valence 2 with two lone pairs) and two hydrogens H_1, H_2 (2 strands each) — in H_{28}(q), by the assembly projector e_{\lambda,\mu} over the parabolic subalgebra H_\lambda(q) with strand-partition \lambda = (24, 2, 2).
rem:h2o-molecular-braid-remark:
Remark Bonding generators and symmetry of the water braid. Of the H_\lambda(q) generators, the N - k = 25 intra-block generators are internal to the three atoms. The k - 1 = 2 cross-block (bonding) generators are the two O–H \sigma-bonds. The assembly projector selects the Wedderburn block \mu that pairs each hydrogen's electron with oxygen. The formalisation fixed: total N = 28, two bonding generators, and the hydrogen-exchange symmetry of the partition.

Two interpretations follow. First, the molecular point symmetry acts as the stabiliser of e_{\lambda,\mu}. Second, the lone pairs of oxygen force a bent geometry.
rem:h2o-c2v-from-projector:
Remark C_{2v} as the stabiliser of the H₂O assembly projector. Interpretation of the H_2O molecular braid.

The two hydrogen sub-units of water carry equal strand counts. The exchange H_1 \leftrightarrow H_2 fixes the strand-partition \lambda = (24,2,2) and hence the assembly projector e_{\lambda,\mu}. That S_2 stabiliser is the C_{2v} point symmetry of the molecule — a C_2 rotation about the bisector of the H–O–H angle, fixing oxygen.

This instantiates the general principle that a structure's point symmetry is the stabiliser of its assembly projector. The same mechanism gives benzene's three equal acetylene units the ring symmetry S_3 (via e_{(2,2,2),(6)}). Water and benzene are the S_2 and S_3 instances of one categorical statement. The same reading, applied to the inter-molecular operator that forms a condensed phase, extends the principle from molecular point groups to the symmetries of phases of matter.
rem:h2o-bent-geometry:
Remark Bent geometry and the four hydrogen-bond directions. Interpretation of the H_2O molecular braid.

Oxygen contributes two bonding sites and two lone pairs. In the assembly, the lone pairs occupy two of the four tetrahedral directions around oxygen as non-bonding phantom sites. This is the NH_3 \to H_2O extension of the methane T_d optimisation. Lone-pair repulsion relaxes the H–O–H angle from the ideal 109.5^\circ toward the observed \approx 104.5^\circ.

The four directions — two donor H and two acceptor lone pairs — provide the per-molecule input to the ice lattice. Each water molecule hydrogen-bonds to four neighbours, two as donor and two as acceptor. The resulting tetrahedral coordination tiles into hexagonal ice I_h (space group P6_3/mmc). The open tetrahedral network explains why ice is less dense than liquid water. The ice rule requires every bond to hold exactly one hydrogen. Which two of the four bonds carry this molecule's hydrogens is then the categorical origin of the Pauling residual entropy of ice, \approx R\ln(3/2). The detailed tiling and its symmetry are developed in the phase-symmetry model.
prop:tetrahedral-hbond-directions:
Proposition The four H-bond directions are tetrahedral (\cos\theta_0 = -1/3). The four hydrogen-bond directions of a water in ice — two donor, two acceptor — point to the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. Taking the vertex vectors (\pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1) with an even number of minus signs, they sum to zero, each has squared length 3, and any two have dot product -1. The bond-angle cosine is

 \cos\theta_0 \;=\; \frac{u_i \cdot u_j}{|u_i|\,|u_j|} \;=\; \frac{-1}{3}, \qquad \theta_0 = \arccos\!\left(-\tfrac13\right) \approx 109.47^\circ.

This is the symmetric reference angle \theta_0 from which oxygen's lone pairs displace the H–O–H angle to \approx 104.5^\circ (the quadratic-well shift). The four facts — balanced sum, squared length 3, pairwise dot -1, and \cos\theta_0 = -1/3 — hold exactly over \mathbb{R}.
prop:h2o-bond-angle-shift:
Proposition Bent angle as a quadratic-well shift. Near the symmetric tetrahedral value \theta_0, the bond-bending energy of water is harmonic — a quadratic restoring term a(\theta-\theta_0)^2 with stiffness a > 0 — and oxygen's two lone pairs add a linear perturbation b\,\theta. The energy a(\theta-\theta_0)^2 + b\,\theta is minimised at

 \theta_{\min} \;=\; \theta_0 - \frac{b}{2a},

which is a linear response of the quadratic minimum. For water b > 0 (the lone-pair term penalises the wider symmetric angle), so \theta_{\min} < \theta_0. The reduction 109.5^\circ \to 104.5^\circ is the quadratic well's minimum displaced by the lone-pair term. The sign of the shift is structural. Its magnitude b/(2a) is the lone-pair repulsion strength relative to the angular stiffness.
prf:h2o-bond-angle-shift: Proof Proof of h2o bond angle shift. Writing b = 2as, the energy minus its value at \theta_0 - s is the perfect square a\bigl(\theta - (\theta_0 - s)\bigr)^2 \ge 0, so \theta_0 - s = \theta_0 - b/(2a) is the global minimiser. \qquad\blacksquare
prop:symmetric-block-domain-weight:
Proposition Symmetric-block domain weight: lone/bond = q^2. On the symmetric (trivial) representation of the braid monoid — the one-dimensional Wedderburn block that a molecule's C_{nv} assembly projector selects (the S_n-symmetric channel of C_{2v} as the stabiliser of the H₂O assembly projector) — every generator \sigma_i acts as the scalar q. Hence an electron domain represented by a braid word w of length \ell has weight

  w_{\mathrm{domain}} = q^{\ell}.

In particular, the lone pair e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (length 3) and the \sigma-bond (length 1) have weights q^3 and q, so the lone-pair to bond weight ratio is

  \frac{w_{\mathrm{lone}}}{w_{\mathrm{bond}}} = \frac{q^3}{q} = q^2 .

This ratio is derived as a ratio of Hecke eigenvalues on the symmetric channel, without central-atom input or fitting. Being a ratio of eigenvalues rather than an angle, it is independent of the repulsion kernel. The provable core — the weight law q^{\ell} and the corollary q^3 = q^2\cdot q — is proved in full.
rem:domain-weight-vsepr-angles: Remark Bond angles from the q^{\ell} domain weight.
conj:h2s-angle-s3-braid-holonomy:
Conjecture H₂S bond-angle residual = chiral S^3 braid holonomy. The bond-angle residual of \mathrm{H_2S} — the opening \Delta\theta \approx +2.1^\circ of the H–S–H angle above the pure-p base \theta_0 = 90^\circ — equals the q-deformed Chern–Simons holonomy (the monodromy phase around the singular fibre \zeta_\ell) of the chiral 3p_z lone-pair braid \beta_{3p_z} on the chirality cell — the signed-content-zero standard Wedderburn block V_{(2,1)} (the q-Dirac kernel D_q^2(\lambda)=0):

  \Delta\theta_{\mathrm{H_2S}}
  \;=\;
  \arg \mathrm{Res}_{q=\zeta_\ell}\!\Bigl[\,\Phi_q \cdot
        \mathrm{tr}_{M,(2,1)}\bigl(\beta_{3p_z}\bigr)\Bigr].

Equivalently, \Delta\theta is the bar-anti-symmetric (P_{\mathrm{skew}}, odd-in-h) part of the chiral lone's S^3 braid holonomy. This is the chiral channel the framework otherwise projects away. It vanishes for the bar-symmetric (self-dual, palindromic) lone pairs of \mathrm{H_2O}, which is why \mathrm{H_2O}'s angle is the clean q^2 prediction with no residual.
prop:ice-pauling-residual:
Proposition Pauling residual entropy of ice: W_1 = 3/2. In ice I_h each water molecule is hydrogen-bonded to four neighbours — two as donor (its two H's) and two as acceptor (its two lone pairs), the four directions of the H_2O braid. Subject to the ice rule that every bond carries exactly one hydrogen, the per-molecule multiplicity is

 W_1 \;=\; \binom{4}{2}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{2} \;=\; \frac{6}{4} \;=\; \frac{3}{2},

thus the molar residual entropy is S = R\ln\tfrac32 \approx 3.37\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} (Pauling, 1935). This agrees closely with the measured ice calorimetry.
prf:ice-pauling-residual: Proof Proof of ice pauling residual. A water assigns its two donated hydrogens among its four bonds in \binom{4}{2}=6 ways; each of its two bonds is shared with a neighbour and, on the independent estimate, carries exactly one hydrogen with probability \tfrac12, giving W_1 = 6\cdot(\tfrac12)^2 = \tfrac32. The identities \binom{4}{2}=6 and \binom{4}{2}(\tfrac12)^2 = \tfrac32 hold exactly over \mathbb{Q}; the entropy S = Nk\ln W_1 = R\ln\tfrac32 is the archimedean evaluation. \qquad\blacksquare
sec:benzene-computation-intro: Benzene closes the chapter with a genuinely new structural feature. Benzene C_6H_6 as a molecular braid arranges six carbons in a ring on twelve strands, with \pi-electrons spread across the cycle rather than localised on alternating bonds. The LP dual prefers the threading link T(2,6) over any Kekulé alternation. This D_6 symmetry of the threading link is read as the experimental fact that all six C{-}C bonds have equal length. Aromaticity here is not an extra postulate but a forced output of the LP minimum on an n-membered ring.
def:benzene-molecular-braid: Definition Benzene C_6H_6 as a molecular braid. Benzene C_6H_6 is the molecular braid of six carbon atoms and six hydrogen atoms, assembled iteratively from pre-computed atomic braids, with six C--C \sigma bonds and six C--H \sigma bonds (single, one shared pair each) and six \pi electrons delocalized around the ring.
rem:benzene-molecular-braid-remark: Remark Strand count and iterative construction of benzene.
prop:benzene-threading-emergence: Proposition Threading link T(2,6) emerges as the LP-optimal \pi configuration. Conditional on Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients. The LP dual of the benzene molecular braid in H_{120}(q) selects the threading link T(2, 6) = (\sigma_1\sigma_2 \cdots \sigma_5)^2 as the optimal \pi-electron configuration.
rem:benzene-threading-selection:
Remark Why the threading link is LP-optimal, and the resonance energy. After the \sigma-bond framework is assembled, there remain 6 unpaired electrons — one from each carbon's 2p_z orbital. The LP dual of Threading link T(2,6) emerges as the LP-optimal \pi configuration optimises their placement.

Candidate configurations:

Configuration Braid structure Shared crossings
3 alternating double bonds (Kekulé) 3 localised \pi pairs 3 \times 2 = 6
Threading link T(2, 6) Non-local torus link 6 \times 2 = 12
2 Dewar bonds + 1 double Mixed localised Variable

The threading link is selected because:

  1. More shared crossings. T(2, 6) creates 12 attractive \sigma^{-1} crossings (each of the 6 \pi electrons has attractive crossings with 2 adjacent carbon protons), compared to only 6 for localised Kekulé double bonds.
  2. D_6 symmetry. The threading link has full hexagonal symmetry. It minimises inter-electron repulsion by distributing the 6 \pi electrons uniformly around the ring.
  3. Alexander polynomial weight. The Alexander polynomial \Delta_{T(2,6)}(q) = (q^3 - q^{-3})/(q - q^{-1}) = [3]_{q^2} gives the threading link half the Alexander weight of pairwise bonding, reducing \Phi_1 relative to localised bonds.

The \Phi_1 comparison:

  \Phi_1^{T(2,6)} < \Phi_1^{\text{Kekulé}} < \Phi_1^{\text{Dewar}}

The LP dual shadow price for the threading link is the resonance stabilisation energy of benzene:

  E_{\mathrm{res}} = \alpha \bigl(
    \Phi_1^{\text{Kekulé}} - \Phi_1^{T(2,6)}
  \bigr)

The observed resonance energy is \approx 1.56 \;\mathrm{eV} (36 kcal/mol).
rem:benzene-bond-equalization:
Remark Bond equalization from D_6 symmetry of T(2,6). The D_6 symmetry of the threading link T(2, 6) ensures that all six C--C bonds are identical. Each bond has:

  • 1 \sigma pair (from step 1--4 of the construction)
  • \frac{1}{2} \pi pair (from the threading link — each \pi electron is shared between 2 adjacent carbons)

Total bond order per C--C bond is 1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}.

This is the braid-theoretic derivation of the experimentally observed bond order 1.5 in benzene, with equal bond lengths of 1.4\;\text{Å}\;\text{\AA} (between the C--C single bond length 1.54\;\text{Å}\;\text{\AA} and double bond length 1.34\;\text{Å}\;\text{\AA}).

The construction proves that bond equalization is not an axiom of molecular orbital theory but a theorem of the LP dual. The threading link's D_6 symmetry is the unique \Phi_1 minimum for 6 \pi electrons on a 6-membered ring.

This extends to larger aromatics (naphthalene C_{10}H_8, anthracene C_{14}H_{10}) by the same construction. Build the \sigma framework iteratively, then apply the LP dual to select the optimal \pi configuration. The threading link T(2, N) generalises accordingly to N-membered rings, with Alexander polynomial \Delta_{T(2,N)}(q) = (q^{N/2} - q^{-N/2})/(q - q^{-1}) for even N.
rem:benzene-assembly-spine:
Remark The \gamma\gamma-from-light assembly spine to benzene. Light initiates the assembly. The Breit–Wheeler process \gamma\gamma \to e^+e^- seeds a lepton pair. That energy feeds quark–antiquark production, whose confinement closes into the Borromean nucleon and, by meson exchange, the proton. Twelve nucleons bind into a ^{12}\mathrm{C} atom (the A \ge 3 binding closure), and carbon's four octet channels assemble molecules.

The molecular layer is parameter-free. Each covalent bond order is the cardinality of the saturated orthogonal-channel set — the bond order = LP active set identity. The fractional \pi of an aromatic ring is the lateral-\pi overlap of the embeddable knot operator, delocalised by the assembly projector.
rem:assembly-shortest-production:
Remark The assembly path is canonical: shortest word up to symmetry. Retrosynthesis — asking which reactions produce a target — is famously non-unique. For a fixed assembly braid word, the forward categorical assembly is not. The \gamma\gamma-spine has a canonical shortest path: the Hecke normal form of the assembly braid word. This is the shortest representative modulo the braid relations, selected by the confinement min-action program.

The path is unique only up to the molecular symmetry group. Benzene's D_6 permutes the six equivalent acetylene insertions, so the canonical word is a single orbit representative, not a single word. This is the assembly form of the Gröbner–Shirshov picture: many syntactic derivations collapse onto one normal form, and the min-action confinement program picks it. This is the categorical replacement for a standard synthetic route. The uniqueness is confluence of one word. When bond words are re-selected as the bonds form, different bond orders can settle on different stable words, so the assembled product itself need not be unique.
rem:assembly-emission-ledger:
Remark Net-emission ledger: photon (categorical) and phonon (archimedean). Assembling benzene from separated atoms releases the binding energy as a net emission,

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{emit}}
    = \bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\text{final}} - \mathrm{NF}_{\text{initial}}\bigr)\,
      \mathfrak{E}_0 ,

which is the change in normal-form crossing count scaled by the per-crossing energy \mathfrak{E}_0. Ring closure delocalises six \pi electrons. This adds a +\tfrac{1}{2} bond-order increment on each of the six \mathrm{C\!-\!C} bonds (witness benzene-assembly-spine). This sums to three bond-orders of aromatic stabilisation released on closure.

The emission splits into two channels. The photon channel is categorical — the trivial-knot electromagnetic mode, carrying the quantised normal-form change. The phonon channel is archimedean (lattice and thermal). The ledger is partial: the cardinality — the normal-form crossing change, hence the photon channel's quantum content — is robust, but the absolute energy partition between photon and phonon awaits the lateral-\pi overlap weight w_\perp of the embeddable knot operator. This is the same cardinality-robust, energy-pending split that governs the bond model.
def:iterated-confinement-layer:
Definition Confinement layer, confined motif, and functorial column promotion. Let K be a commutative ring equipped with a compatible linear order when inequalities are invoked, and let d, m \in \mathbb{N}.

  1. A confinement layer \mathcal{L} = (A, c, \mathcal{A}) consists of an integer conserved-charge matrix A \in \mathbb{Z}^{d \times m}, a column cost vector c \in K^m defining c(z) := \sum_{j=1}^m z_j c_j on signed configurations z \in \mathbb{Z}^m, and an admissibility predicate \mathcal{A} \subseteq \mathbb{N}^m on nonnegative column multiplicities.
  2. Given dual shadow prices y \in K^d, the reduced cost of column j \in \{1,\dots,m\} is 
      \bar{c}(y)_j := c_j - \sum_{i=1}^d A_{ij} y_i.
  3. A configuration w \in \mathbb{N}^m is a confined motif of \mathcal{L} if w \neq 0, w \in \mathcal{A}, and for every nontrivial decomposition into nonzero admissible configurations u_1, u_2 \in \mathcal{A} \setminus \{0\} satisfying A w = A u_1 + A u_2, strict binding sub-additivity holds: 
      c(w) < c(u_1) + c(u_2).
  4. Given a selected family of m' motifs W = (w_1, \dots, w_{m'}) \in (\mathbb{N}^m)^{m'}, a residual inter-motif cost shift \delta c \in K^{m'}, and a next-layer admissibility predicate \mathcal{A}' \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{m'}, functorial column promotion [dantzig-wolfe1960, benders1962, deloera-hemmecke-koeppe2013] produces the next confinement layer \mathcal{L}' = (A', c', \mathcal{A}') with 
      A'_{i\alpha} := (A w_\alpha)_i,
  \qquad
  c'_\alpha := c(w_\alpha) + \delta c_\alpha
  \qquad (\alpha = 1,\dots,m'),
    and constituent expansion \mathcal{E}_W(v)_j := \sum_{\alpha=1}^{m'} v_\alpha w_{\alpha,j} satisfying A' v = A\,\mathcal{E}_W(v) for all v \in \mathbb{Z}^{m'}.
thm:adiabatic-confinement-gap-stability:
Theorem Reduced-cost fiber invariance, adiabatic gap stability, and cross-layer deconfinement flip. Let \mathcal{L}_k = (A_k, c_k, \mathcal{A}_k) be a confinement layer over a strictly linearly ordered commutative ring K [dantzig-wolfe1960, bloch-horowitz1958, schrieffer-wolff1966].

  1. Conservation-fiber invariance and LP optimality: For every shadow-price vector y \in K^{d_k} and any two configurations u, v \in \mathbb{Z}^{m_k} in the same conservation fiber A_k u = A_k v, 
      \bar{c}_k(y)(u - v) = c_k(u - v).
    If u^* \in \mathbb{N}^{m_k} satisfies A_k u^* = b, \bar{c}_k(y^*)_j \ge 0, and u^*_j \bar{c}_k(y^*)_j = 0 for all j, then c_k(u^*) = b^\top y^* \le c_k(u) for every u \in \mathbb{N}^{m_k} with A_k u = b.
  2. Adiabatic confinement stability: Let g \in \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_k) be an intra-layer motif-fission move satisfying c_k(g) \ge \Delta_k > 0, and let \delta_V(g) \in K be the residual Layer-(k+1) cost perturbation on g. If |\delta_V(g)| < \Delta_k (equivalently, over a linearly ordered field, \eta_k := |\delta_V(g)| / \Delta_k < 1), then 
      c_k(g) + \delta_V(g) > 0,
    with lower margin c_k(g) + \delta_V(g) \ge \Delta_k - |\delta_V(g)| > 0.
  3. Cross-layer deconfinement flip: Conversely, if c_k(g) \le \Delta_k and an external chemical potential or Fermi pressure drives -\delta_V(g) > \Delta_k, then 
      c_k(g) + \delta_V(g) < 0.
rem:five-layer-confinement-tower-rg:
Remark The five-layer iterated confinement tower as zero-counterterm algebraic renormalization. Iterating functorial column promotion produces a five-layer physical tower \mathcal{L}_0 \to \mathcal{L}_1 \to \mathcal{L}_2 \to \mathcal{L}_3 \to \mathcal{L}_4 governed at each step by a single dimensionless adiabatic ratio \eta_k = \|V_{k+1}\| / \Delta_k evaluated from (m_e, q_0) without fitted counterterms:

Transition Confined motifs promoted Unperturbed gap \Delta_k Next-layer coupling \|V_{k+1}\| Adiabatic ratio \eta_k Physical regime
\mathcal{L}_0 \to \mathcal{L}_1 Elementary B_3 ribbon words \mapsto colour-singlet hadrons (p, n, \pi) m_p(q_0) \approx 938.27\,\mathrm{MeV} Radiative QED dressing \alpha m_p 7.30 \times 10^{-3} Electroweak / QED isospin splitting
\mathcal{L}_1 \to \mathcal{L}_2 Nucleons (p,n) \mapsto bound nuclei (Z, N_{\mathrm{nuc}}) m_p(q_0) \approx 938.27\,\mathrm{MeV} B({}^{12}\mathrm{C})/12 \approx 7.68\,\mathrm{MeV} 8.19 \times 10^{-3} 1\%–5\% EMC structure-function shift without quark deconfinement [aubert-emc1983]
\mathcal{L}_2 \to \mathcal{L}_3 Frozen nuclei (Z,N_{\mathrm{nuc}}) \mapsto neutral atoms and ions (Z, N_e) B({}^{12}\mathrm{C})/12 \approx 7.68\,\mathrm{MeV} \mathrm{Ry} = \frac{1}{2}\alpha^2 m_e \approx 13.61\,\mathrm{eV} 1.77 \times 10^{-6} Complete nuclear conservation across ambient chemistry

thm:toric-diophantine-stoichiometry:
Theorem Diophantine reaction kernel, Hess's law, toric binomials, and canonical stoichiometric circuits. Let A_{\mathrm{chem}} \in \mathbb{Z}^{E \times M} be the elemental stoichiometry matrix of M molecular species over E conserved Layer-\mathcal{L}_2 nuclear elements, and let R be any commutative ring [deloera-hemmecke-koeppe2013, sturmfels-thomas1997, craciun-dickenstein-shiu-sturmfels2009].

  1. Diophantine kernel and lattice closure: Unsigned reactant and product multiplicities \nu_-, \nu_+ \in \mathbb{N}^M conserve every element (\sum_{j=1}^M A_{\mathrm{chem},ej}\nu_{-,j} = \sum_{j=1}^M A_{\mathrm{chem},ej}\nu_{+,j} for all e) if and only if the signed stoichiometric vector v := \nu_+ - \nu_- satisfies A_{\mathrm{chem}} v = 0. For all v_1, v_2 \in \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}}) and a, b \in \mathbb{Z}, a v_1 + b v_2 \in \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}}), reaction enthalpy \Delta H(v) := h_f(v) satisfies \Delta H(a v_1 + b v_2) = a\,\Delta H(v_1) + b\,\Delta H(v_2) = \bar{h}_f(y)(a v_1 + b v_2) for all elemental reference potentials y \in R^E, and every sequence of balanced reactions preserves A_{\mathrm{chem}} n = b.
  2. Toric binomial vanishing: For every balanced reaction \nu_+ - \nu_- \in \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}}) and every elemental fugacity tuple t \in (R^\times)^E, the monomial evaluation x_j(t) := \prod_{e=1}^E t_e^{A_{\mathrm{chem},ej}} satisfies 
      x(t)^{\nu_+} - x(t)^{\nu_-} = 0.
  3. Canonical rank-1 primitive circuits: The integer kernels \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}}) of water synthesis (\mathrm{H}_2,\mathrm{O}_2,\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}), methane combustion (\mathrm{CH}_4,\mathrm{O}_2,\mathrm{CO}_2,\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}), Haber–Bosch ammonia synthesis (\mathrm{N}_2,\mathrm{H}_2,\mathrm{NH}_3), and glucose respiration (\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6,\mathrm{O}_2,\mathrm{CO}_2,\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}) are free rank-1 \mathbb{Z}-modules generated respectively by the primitive circuits (-2,-1,2), (-1,-2,1,2), (-1,-3,2), and (-1,-6,6,6).
  4. Complete \mathbb{Z}-basis of the seven-species \mathrm{C}\text{--}\mathrm{H}\text{--}\mathrm{O} network: On (\mathrm{C},\mathrm{H}_2,\mathrm{O}_2,\mathrm{CO},\mathrm{CO}_2,\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O},\mathrm{CH}_4), \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}}) \cong \mathbb{Z}^4 is spanned over \mathbb{Z} by water–gas shift (0,1,0,-1,1,-1,0), Boudouard disproportionation (1,0,0,-2,1,0,0), carbon-monoxide methanation (0,-3,0,-1,0,1,1), and carbon oxidation (-1,0,-1,0,1,0,0).
rem:toric-chemical-groebner-geometry: Remark Gröbner test sets, Sturmfels–Thomas enthalpy normal forms, and Birch mass-action toric equilibria. Because \eta_2 \approx 1.77 \times 10^{-6} \ll 1, Layer \mathcal{L}_2 nuclear cores remain invariant across ambient chemical transformations, reducing molecular reaction stoichiometry to integer lattice geometry and toric commutative algebra [deloera-hemmecke-koeppe2013, craciun-dickenstein-shiu-sturmfels2009].
prose:outro-molecular-construction:
Chapter close — Molecular Construction from Nucleon Braids.

This closes the molecular-construction chapter. Covalent bonds have been lifted from the chemical literature into categorical morphisms in \mathbf{C}. The diatomic \mathrm{H}_2 case was worked through in detail. The benzene-ring example exhibits the ring-closure pattern that the next chapter generalises to arbitrary carbon backbones.

The next chapter (organic chemistry) extends the construction to the full Hopf-chain taxonomy of organic molecules: aliphatic chains, aromatic rings, and the comparative energetics that distinguish linear from cyclic isomers. The categorical machinery developed here — bond morphisms, ring-closure cocycles, threading transitions — carries over without modification. The next chapter surveys its applications rather than introduces new constructions.
sec:covalent-bonding-intro:
Where metallic bonding shares residual sub-links across an entire lattice, molecular chemistry localises the sharing between two atoms. This is made precise as a covalent bond of order k: a shared sub-Hopf link of k trefoils simultaneously linked to one open site in each partner. Single, double, and triple bonds are read off as k = 1, 2, 3. Each increment in bond order adds one shared trefoil, so higher bond order registers as additional rigidity. The explicit crossing-energy formula is stated in the covalent-bond definition.

The section closes by partitioning carbon's electron cloud into a closed 1s^2 pair and a residual sub-link of size four. This four-site residual link is exactly half-filling of the second shell's capacity. This places carbon at the maximally covalent midpoint of the metallic-character spectrum.
def:covalent-bond-types:
Definition Covalent bond (shared Hopf links). Let \mathcal{A}_1 and \mathcal{A}_2 be atoms with residual sub-links R_1 and R_2. In agreement with covalent bond via shared electron braids, each valence electron is the three-strand word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 whose closure is the positive Hopf link T(2,2) (with the single-component trefoil T_{2,3} retained as the alternative model). A covalent bond of order k is a shared sub-Hopf link

  B_k(R_1, R_2)
  = 
  \underbrace{e^- \oplus \cdots \oplus e^-}_{k \text{ shared electrons } (T(2,2)\text{ closures})}

where each shared electron closure is simultaneously Hopf-linked to one open site in R_1 and one open site in R_2. The integer k is the bond order. The crossing energy of the bond is

  E_{\mathrm{bond}}(k)
  = 
  k \cdot \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(T(2,2)) +
  \binom{k}{2}  \Delta E_{\mathrm{inter}},

where T(2,2) is the Hopf link and \Delta E_{\mathrm{inter}} is the inter-link interaction within the shared sub-link.
rem:covalent-bond-types-remark:
Remark Single, double and triple bonds.

Bond order k Chemical name Shared electrons (T(2,2) closures) Linking sites consumed
1 Single bond 1 1 per atom
2 Double bond 2 2 per atom
3 Triple bond 3 3 per atom

In the crossing energy E_{\mathrm{bond}}(k), the first term accounts for k individual Hopf links, and the second for inter-link interactions within the shared sub-link. Higher bond order increases both binding strength and rigidity: a triple bond is stronger and stiffer than a single bond because the three shared electron closures form a coupled sub-link that resists Reidemeister moves.
rem:carbon-valence:
Remark Carbon's four open linking sites. Carbon (p = 6) has electron cloud 6 \cdot T_{2,3} partitioned as

  \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{C}}
  = 
  \underbrace{T_{2,3} \oplus T_{2,3}}_{\text{closed } 1s^2}
   \oplus 
  \underbrace{T_{2,3} \oplus T_{2,3} \oplus T_{2,3} \oplus T_{2,3}}_{\text{residual } R,  |R| = 4}.

The second shell has capacity 2 \cdot 2^2 = 8, so the residual sub-link R occupies exactly half the available linking sites: |R| / 2n^2 = 4/8 = 1/2.

This half-filling makes carbon unique among the light elements:

  1. Maximal bonding capacity: 4 open linking sites. More than any other period-2 element.
  2. Symmetric energy landscape: adding a trefoil and removing a trefoil cost comparable crossing energy. Carbon shares electrons via covalent bonds.
  3. Chain-forming ability: with 4 sites, carbon can bond to two neighbours while retaining 2 sites for branching. This is the topological origin of organic chemistry's combinatorial richness.

The residual linking number \lambda(R) = 4 places carbon in the middle of the metallic character spectrum. It is maximally covalent, sitting between the metallic and the inert extremes.
